reason: Same as Round 2's logic, applied to the concentrated/leveraged expression: nothing in today's research (2026-09-19) breaks the thesis on any of the four legs, so a replacement book would only add leverage-adjusted turnover cost without changing the exposure that's actually working. SOXL is up +18.95% on this leg alone and semis (SMH) still closed +2.21% on 9/18 near 52-week highs - there is a rotation-away-from-chips narrative in circulation, which is worth flagging, but price has not confirmed it yet, and a single day's headline is not enough to unwind a 3x leveraged momentum position mid-trend. BTC spot reclaimed $80k and printed +4.12% in the last 24h after working through CLARITY Act-related selling, with $180M of shorts liquidated on the move - the highest-conviction leg in the book is strengthening, not weakening. GUSH (leveraged E&P) pulled back -2.08% on 9/18 even as Brent traded above $100/bbl on Middle East supply risk; that's a one-day wobble inside a sector still up ~86% YTD, not a trend break, so it does not justify cutting the position. XLU short remains right at its 52-week low, down again on 9/18, with the underlying negative-momentum thesis (rate-sensitive defensives lagging) still confirming. No leg shows a reversal signal strong enough to justify realizing the SOXL gain or resetting the book, and this book's own novelty rule would in any case require staying well clear of Round 2's five other symbols, which a hold trivially satisfies since composition is unchanged.
